input.name: images
notes: Square input only. Export rejects a non-square imgsz, and height equals width, 640 by default.
The image is not scaled to fill the canvas. The longest side goes to R = min(636, height, width), so 636 at 640 x 640.
Scale by r = min(R / h, R / w) and resize to (round(w * r), round(h * r)). The rounding is Python round, so an exact .5 goes to the even neighbor.
Paste the resized image onto a canvas filled with 114 at left = (width - new_w) // 2 and top = (height - new_h) // 2.
On the test image, cv2.resize with INTER_LINEAR loses two of the eight detections, and INTER_AREA moves boxes by up to 1.4 px.
Divide by 255 after the resize. There is no mean or std normalization.

outputs.name: pred_logits
outputs.meaning: Boxes, despite the name. x1, y1, x2, y2 in input-canvas pixels. anchors is the cell count over strides 8, 16 and 32, 8400 at 640 x 640.

outputs.name: pred_boxes
outputs.meaning: Class scores, despite the name. Sigmoid already applied. 80 classes for the COCO checkpoints.

postprocess: The output names are swapped relative to their content. Read boxes from pred_logits and scores from pred_boxes, or tell them apart by the last dimension (4 for boxes).
Take the best class per anchor: score = max over classes, class = argmax. One anchor yields at most one detection.
Keep anchors whose score is strictly above the confidence threshold (0.25 by default).
Keep the 1000 highest scoring candidates.
Map boxes back to the original image: subtract left from x and top from y, divide by r, clip to the image. Drop boxes left with zero width or height.
Run NMS per class with IoU 0.45 and keep at most 300 detections.
nms=True is not available for this family: export raises NotImplementedError.

input.name: images
notes: Square input only. Export rejects a non-square imgsz, and height equals width, 640 by default.
Channels are BGR, unlike detection. Pad value and position also differ from detection.
The longest side goes to R = min(640, height, width), so it fills the canvas.
Scale by r = min(R / h, R / w) and resize to (round(w * r), round(h * r)). The rounding is Python round, so an exact .5 goes to the even neighbor.
Paste the resized image in the top-left corner of a canvas filled with 127. All padding is on the bottom and the right.
On the test image, cv2.resize with INTER_LINEAR or INTER_AREA moves boxes by up to 5 px and keypoints by more than 10 px.
Divide by 255 after the resize. There is no mean or std normalization.

outputs.name: boxes
outputs.meaning: Person boxes as x1, y1, x2, y2 in input-canvas pixels. anchors is the cell count over strides 8, 16 and 32, 8400 at 640 x 640.

outputs.name: scores
outputs.meaning: Class scores, sigmoid already applied. nc is 1 (person) for the COCO pose checkpoints.

outputs.name: keypoints_xy
outputs.meaning: Keypoint x, y in input-canvas pixels. num_keypoints is 17 (COCO order) for the COCO pose checkpoints.

outputs.name: keypoints_conf
outputs.meaning: Per-keypoint visibility score, sigmoid already applied.

postprocess: Take the best class per anchor: score = max over classes, class = argmax. With one class this is just the person score.
Keep anchors whose score is at or above the confidence threshold (0.25 by default). This is >=, not > as in detection.
Keep the 1000 highest scoring candidates.
Map boxes and keypoints back to the original image: divide x and y by r. The image sits in the top-left corner, so there is no pad offset to subtract.
Clip boxes to the image and drop boxes left with zero width or height. Keypoints are not clipped and can fall outside the image.
Run NMS per class with IoU 0.45 and keep at most 300 detections. Keep each survivor's keypoints as (x, y, keypoints_conf).
nms=True is not available for this family: export raises NotImplementedError.

input.name: images
notes: Square input only. Export rejects a non-square imgsz, and height equals width, 1024 by default.
Channels are BGR, unlike detection. The resize filter and the pad position also differ from detection.
The longest side goes to R = min(1024, height, width), so it fills the canvas.
Scale by r = min(R / h, R / w) and resize to (round(w * r), round(h * r)). The rounding is Python round, so an exact .5 goes to the even neighbor.

The resize is cv2.resize with INTER_LINEAR, not Pillow as in detection and pose. It is skipped when the image already has that size. On the test image, Pillow's filter here changes the detection count.
Paste the resized image in the top-left corner of a canvas filled with 114. All padding is on the bottom and the right.
Divide by 255 after the resize. There is no mean or std normalization.

outputs.name: boxes
outputs.meaning: Rotated boxes as cx, cy, w, h, angle. cx, cy, w and h are in input-canvas pixels. The angle is in radians. The graph computes it as (sigmoid(logit) - 0.25) x pi, so it lies between -pi/4 and 3pi/4 and is not wrapped yet. The w side points along (cos angle, sin angle) in image coordinates, y down. anchors is the cell count over strides 8, 16 and 32, 21504 at 1024 x 1024.

outputs.name: scores
outputs.meaning: Class scores, sigmoid already applied. 18 classes (DOTA 2.0) for the published checkpoints.

postprocess: Take the best class per anchor: score = max over classes, class = argmax. One anchor yields at most one detection.
Keep anchors whose score is at or above the confidence threshold (0.25 by default). This is >=, not > as in detection.
Keep the 1000 highest scoring candidates.
Map boxes back to the original image: divide cx, cy, w and h by r. The image sits in the top-left corner, so there is no pad offset, and the angle does not change.
Clip cx to 0 to the image width and cy to 0 to the image height. w and h are not clipped. Drop boxes with w or h at or below 0.
Put the long side first: if h > w, swap w and h and add pi/2 to the angle. Then wrap the angle to [-pi/2, pi/2) with angle = ((angle + pi/2) mod pi) - pi/2.

Run greedy NMS per class on exact rotated-box IoU (polygon intersection area over union, for example cv2.rotatedRectangleIntersection) with IoU 0.45, and keep at most 300 detections. LibreYOLO does not use upstream's matrix soft-NMS.

LibreYOLO also reports an axis-aligned box per detection. With ex = abs(cos angle) * w / 2 + abs(sin angle) * h / 2 and ey = abs(sin angle) * w / 2 + abs(cos angle) * h / 2, it is cx - ex, cy - ey, cx + ex, cy + ey, clipped to the image.
nms=True is not available for this family: export raises NotImplementedError.
